subject: dragonfly
pitch: An emperor dragonfly hovering above a pond. A long, slim abdomen in electric blue with black markings down its back, an apple-green thorax, huge wraparound turquoise eyes, and four glassy wings with a fine net of dark veins and a faint golden sheen, held flat and wide. Six thin legs are tucked under it.
reasoning:
I'm planning a single TypeScript module with the SDK, aiming to keep it concise but high-quality, and thinking through realistic proportions for a hovering dragonfly model based on an emperor dragonfly's actual body length and wingspan.

Now I'm working out how to position the model so its lowest point sits just above the ground, with the body facing forward and wings spread flat and wide in a horizontal plane above the thorax, then setting up the joint hierarchy starting from the root body and abdomen chain.

For the abdomen, I'm shaping it as a long tapering tail from the thorax rear to the tip, with coloring based on blue bands plus black dorsal stripe sectors defined by angle and position ranges along the segment, making sure the sectors don't overlap where they meet.

I'm now sketching out the actual joint hierarchy and coordinates—thorax, head, and a tail chain running from near the thorax rear back along -Z, defining positions in meters for each joint.

For the tail chain I'm setting up a simple two-point straight path split into 8 evenly spaced joints, letting the chain helper compute aim and up frames automatically along that line. Then I'm thinking through the abdomen radius taper function to give it a slim shape with some swelling along its length.

For coloring I'm planning electric blue sweep with black dorsal sectors at specific t-ranges to mimic segmented banding, then working out how to add the small black cerci spikes at the tail tip using a base point and direction near the last tail joint.

For the thorax, I'm switching to a loft shape with stations at varying widths and heights along the z-axis to build an apple-green, ellipsoid-like body that tapers at both ends, blending smoothly into the egg-shaped emperor thorax silhouette.

For the eyes, I'm placing two large turquoise spheres symmetrically on either side of the head to create that huge, wraparound dragonfly-eye look.

Then I'm positioning the head bone just behind the eyes, since the eyes themselves will cover most of the head area, and moving on to plan the four wings — forewing and hindwing on each side, matching an emperor dragonfly's structure.

Figuring out wing geometry now: thin card shapes anchored at the thorax with vein textures, orienting them horizontally outward and slightly forward using frame-based flow and lean parameters to control how each card's spine extends.

Using light glassy tint for the alphaTest material. Each side gets a forewing and hindwing card, with the hindwing slightly broader at base; given an emperor dragonfly's roughly 11cm wingspan, each wing runs about 0.05m from body, so I'm placing the wing roots around x=±0.008 to ±0.058 with card length 0.05 centered accordingly.

Now I'm setting card width (0.012 forewing, 0.014 hindwing) running from root to root+h along the spine, and mapping texture UVs so the SVG's bottom edge corresponds to the wing root and top edge to the tip, with viewBox sized to match each card's aspect ratio. I'm sketching the actual wing silhouette path in SVG coordinates, narrowing from the root at the bottom to a rounded tip near the top using curve segments.

Writing SVG vein pattern...

I'm deciding to layer a translucent pale-blue fill with a golden gradient overlay for sheen, and noting the card rendering will multiply this texture by a white tint so the drawn colors show through unaltered.

Since alpha cutting removes anything below 0.5, I need to bump fill-opacity to at least 0.6 so the wing membrane survives rendering, keeping veins fully opaque for crispness. For the actual geometry, I'm setting up four wing cards (forewing and hindwing per side), mirroring texture flow direction between the left and right sides, and orienting each wing frame flat along the Y axis to mimic how dragonflies hold their wings.

I'm positioning wing roots slightly above the body axis and offsetting forewings forward of hindwings, with subtle outward sweep angles for a natural flat, wide stance. Now I'm moving on to the legs — planning six thin tucked legs in three pairs per side, each needing their own chain and placement logic to sit naturally under the body.

For the legs, I'm setting up three-joint chains (hip, knee, foot) with thin black sweep radii, parented to the thorax, and starting to define the actual coordinate points for the leg paths.

Finishing hip-knee-foot coordinates for the hind leg, then mirroring each leg pair across the X axis and naming joints like hipFL, kneeFL, footFL so the chains build correctly. Now I'm planning the wing geometry as four card meshes for the fore and hind wings on each side.

Writing wing card definitions...

For the thorax, I'm thinking apple green with blue stripe markings, probably using a mottle paint function for simplicity, and confirming loft accepts Paint types for coloring sweeps. For the abdomen's black dorsal markings, I'm working out sector angle ranges centered on the dorsal top position.

I need to be careful that a full-length dorsal black stripe sector and the narrower ranged segment-band sectors don't overlap at their boundaries, since sectors can only touch where stretches meet but not overlap -- so I may need to restructure these into non-overlapping t-ranges rather than mixing a full-length entry with discrete banded ones.

Writing abdomen segment pattern...

Now I'm positioning the head's eye spheres, placing them close together near the top of the head so they overlap slightly at the center, giving a wraparound look, and picking turquoise mottled colors for them.

Then I'm setting up the joint hierarchy, adding a thorax root joint and attaching a head joint parented to it, and wiring the eyes and wings to the thorax bone for weighting. Finally I'm defining the thorax's loft stations along the z-axis, each with width and height values to shape the body's cross-section.

Now I'm adding small claspers as spikes at the tail tip, branching outward in opposite directions from a base point near the abdomen's end.

For the wing, I'm generating an SVG with longitudinal veins converging toward a narrower tip, plus cross-veins connecting them, to give the wing a realistic branching structure.

Still tuning the wing width formula...

Setting the gradient stops with warm amber and icy blue tones, keeping opacity above the alpha threshold for the texture fill, and confirming the SVG viewBox is set correctly without explicit width/height attributes.

I'm adding a small dark pterostigma rectangle near each forewing tip for detail, then setting up the leg chains with hip, knee, and foot joints parented to the thorax.

Now I'm sweeping cylindrical tubes along each leg's polyline to give them thickness, and setting up the wing frames and necessary imports before writing the exported build function with its metadata.

I'm checking that the body's lowest leg points still sit above the hover plane, then defining the color palette and writing the abdomen's paint function to create banded segments with a dorsal black stripe pattern.

Still writing paint logic...

I'm verifying that the surface coordinates passed into the paint function correctly represent the dorsal angle and segment position, then setting up the tail chain with eight joints for the abdomen.

For the thorax loft, I'm making sure it binds to the thorax joint since that's the only joint created at the time of its definition, with other joints like the head and legs following afterward.

Now I'm placing the eye spheres relative to the head bone with mottled turquoise paint, keeping their positions and radii small enough to sit cleanly on the head without overlapping too much with the thorax front. Then I work out the wing root positions on the thorax top, sizing the forewings and hindwings separately and setting their flow directions and z-offsets so the hindwing sits slightly behind and below the forewing.

Writing wing SVG outline code...

Adjusting vein spacing to stay within outline...

Writing SVG gradient code...

I need to check orientation carefully—the texture's top edge corresponds to the tip, with the root at the bottom, so the UV coordinates should align with the card's spine starting at the root.

Now I'm verifying the builder API's method signatures (joints, chains, sweeps, lofts, parts, spikes, cards) to make sure names and roles don't collide, and I'm defining the abdomen's radius taper function so it narrows smoothly toward the tip. I'm also placing joints for the thorax, head, legs, and tail, then adding clasper spikes with specific positions and directions.

Working out the leg geometry and chain definitions...

Now setting up wing card placements with mirrored flow vectors for left and right sides, double-checking the frame direction and lean angle math so the wing sheen cards orient correctly.

The eye spheres get their own geometry and mottled turquoise/teal coloring, parented under the head bone. I'll finalize the thorax stripe details and write out the complete code concisely.
